// diagnostic

E0151

`{state}` is not a declared state of `{type}`.

What

`{state}` is not a declared state of `{type}`.

Why

Typestate (D-STATE-HOME1=A): `struct {type} { state { … } }` defines the valid state labels; a name not in that set is likely a typo — a phantom state no transition can reach.

Fix

Correct the spelling, or add `{state}` inside `struct {type} { state { … } }`.

Worked example

First UI snapshot mentioning E0151: tests/ui/typestate/unknown_state_in_marker_is_e0151.stderr.

Error [E0151]: `Stuffed` is not a declared state of `Crate`
  --> tests/ui/typestate/unknown_state_in_marker_is_e0151.jet:11:5
    |
 11 |     #State(Stuffed) fn get(self) -[]> Int {
    |     ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
 Why: Typestate: `struct Crate { state { … } }` defines the valid state labels; `Stuffed` is not among them — a typo here would silently create a phantom state that no transition reaches
 Fix: Add `Stuffed` inside `struct Crate { state { … } }`, or correct the spelling
More: jet-lang.dev/e/E0151

Error [E0150]: `get` needs `Crate` in state `Stuffed`, but `b` is in state `Full`
  --> tests/ui/typestate/unknown_state_in_marker_is_e0151.jet:18:13
    |
 18 |     print(b.get())
    |             ^^^
 Why: Typestate: `get` is only valid in state `Stuffed`; calling it in `Full` is the out-of-order-events bug it prevents
 Fix: Transition `b` into state `Stuffed` before calling `get`
More: jet-lang.dev/e/E0150
